lenken.et: From Middle High German lenken, from Old High German lanca, related to Gelenk. Compare English lank (related to link), Hunsrik lenke.

Lende.et: From Middle High German lende, lente, from Old High German lentī, from Proto-Germanic *landį̄.

Lenz.et: From Middle High German lenze, from Old High German lenzo, from Proto-West Germanic *langatīn. Related to English Lent and Dutch lente.

s: a female given name, variant of Magdalena and Helena, popular in the 1990s

Lennart.et: From Swedish and Danish Lennart. A newer variant of the German Leonhard.

s: a diminutive of the female given names Helene and Magdalene
a male given name, a less common variant of Lennart

lenzen.et: From Middle High German lenzen, from lenze (“spring”).

s: to be idle; to hang out
lenzen.et: Backformation from faulenzen (“to be idle”), originally unrelated to Lenz above, but associated with it. Compare the expression fauler Lenz or lauer Lenz (“period of idleness”).

s: to pump out or drain a ship
lenzen.et: 19th century, derived from Dutch lens (“slack, empty”, also “dry”, of a ship).

s: to sail slowly in front the wind
lenzen.et: From Middle Low German lensen. Cognate with Dutch lenzen. Perhaps from the same adjective as under etymology 3, though this is not certain.
